Minerals Department 
Continental Oil Company 1024 South Plumer Avenue Tucson, Arizona 85719
July 12, 1972
Director
Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
Room 4410
Department of the Interior
Washington, D. C. 20240
Gentlemen:
This letter is in protest of Executive Order 11644 which would severly limit the use of off-the-road vehicles on public lands. Although I believe that some restrictions should be placed on off-the-road vehicles to prevent people from indiscriminately tearing up the countryside, little provision has been made for the productive use of such vehicles, such as in the exploration for and development of our mineral and fossil fuel resources.
The proposal that permits be readily available for those people having legitimate reasons for using off-the-road vehicles on public lands is a good one. Thus, constructive use of such vehicles would be encouraged, while at the same time those people obtaining said permits would be more responsible for their actions while using off-the-road vehicles.
Sincerely yours,
R. C. Mebres II Geolopies
